CASE.focal_event: NVIDIA and OpenAI outline a 10-gigawatt infrastructure partnership

company.name: NVIDIA
company.profile: NVIDIA is a U.S. semiconductor and computing-platform company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It designs GPUs and related systems and software for gaming, professional visualization, data centers and automotive applications. Its computing platforms combine processor hardware with software, libraries and developer tools, including CUDA for parallel computing. The company uses external manufacturers to fabricate, assemble and test its products rather than owning semiconductor wafer-fabrication plants. Its results depend on end-market demand, product mix and pricing, development and manufacturing costs, access to manufacturing capacity and the timely introduction and acceptance of new products. This general business description uses information available in its fiscal 2020 annual report; no later product launches, acquisitions, financial results or customer agreements are assumed unless included in the supplied article.

articles.title: NVIDIA and OpenAI outline a 10-gigawatt infrastructure partnership
articles.text: NVIDIA and OpenAI announced a letter of intent for a partnership covering at least 10 gigawatts of NVIDIA computing systems for OpenAI's AI infrastructure. NVIDIA intends to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI progressively as systems are deployed, including support for data-center and power capacity. The first phase is targeted for the second half of 2026 using NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform. OpenAI would use NVIDIA as a preferred strategic compute and networking partner, and the companies plan to coordinate hardware, software and infrastructure roadmaps. The announcement says the companies expect to finalize details in the coming weeks.

assumptions: The stated economic horizon is an evaluation setting. Announcement dates are treated as available by 23:59:59 UTC on their publication date; exact publication times are not used.
